name: qpdf (CLI, static release binary)
purpose: Baseline repair engine (rewrite with xref reconstruction) and syntactic checker (--check) for the baseline harness and the oracle triad.
last_release: 12.4.2 (tag commit 4eba958, 2026-09-26; same commit as cached SRC-0500)
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/oracle_smoke.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05 in the scratch install: `qpdf '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) q.pdf` -> exit 3, 'qpdf: operation succeeded with warnings; resulting file may have some problems'; `qpdf --check q.pdf` -> exit 0; `qpdf --suppress-recovery '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) qs.pdf` -> exit 2, '... xref not found'. OBS-0500 file: 12.4.2 exit 3 where apt 11.9.0 died with SIGSEGV (OBS-0701). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
rationale: Rewrite produced output on 2/2 files for C1, C2, C3, C6, C7, C8, C9, 1/2 for C5 and 0/2 for C4 and C10 (OBS-0700, smoke test). The latest release no longer segfaults on the OBS-0500 regression file (OBS-0701), so every baseline must pin qpdf >= 12.4.2; the apt 11.9.0 build is not a fair baseline (GAP-009). Best-of option set from qpdf's own manual (SRC-0500 manual/cli.rst): (a) default rewrite, recovery on (CLM-0702); (b) --ignore-xref-streams (cli.rst:680) for xref-stream damage (DMG-005); (c) --decode-level=specialized --object-streams=disable (cli.rst:894, 1069) to surface stream damage; --suppress-recovery only as a strict control. As an oracle, --check is syntax-only by its own manual (CLM-0703): 14 qpdf-clean repaired files were Arlington non-compliant (OBS-0702, GAP-106). pikepdf (TOOL-426) matched qpdf's per-class output exactly (OBS-0700).
alternatives: apt qpdf 11.9.0 (segfaults on a regression file, OBS-0500)

name: MuPDF mutool (clean, draw)
purpose: Baseline repair engine (mutool clean rewrite with repair) and text/render reference for the baseline harness.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/oracle_smoke.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05 after rebuilding the conda-forge env (`micromamba create -c conda-forge mupdf ghostscript poppler`, deleted after the check): `mutool clean -gggg '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) m4.pdf` -> 'warning: repairing PDF document', exit 0, 6-page output; `mutool clean -gggg -s` -> 6 pages; `mutool draw -q -F txt` -> 13,856 bytes. <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
rationale: Copyleft (AGPL): run as a separate binary only, never link or copy code (clean-room rule). The only engine with output on C4 (2/2) and C5 (2/2), but its C4 outputs keep 1 page, so 'produced output' is not fidelity (OBS-0700); no output on C10. Best-of option set from pdfclean.c's usage text (CLM-0704, SRC-0501): clean -gg, clean -gggg, clean -gggg -s (sanitize content streams); -d decompresses for inspection. Tag 1.28.5 is newer than any conda build and was not tested; Stage 4 should build it or use the PyMuPDF wheel's bundled MuPDF (GAP-009).

name: PyMuPDF

Same per-class output as qpdf (OBS-0700); text ratio >= 0.95 of the original on 2/2 for C1, C2, C3, C6, C7, C8 and 0 on C9 and C10. Its page-1 text layer matched PDFium's exactly on all 19 sampled originals (OBS-0708). Renderer for SSIM/LPIPS against PDFium (OBS-0706, GAP-008).

name: pypdfium2 (PDFium)
purpose: Chrome's PDF engine from Python: baseline open/save, text extraction and second renderer for visual metrics.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.visual.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `pypdfium2.PdfDocument('<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2))` -> 6 pages; `PdfDocument.save('pf.pdf')` -> 6-page output; textlayer_coverage.py ran 2026-10-05 (OBS-0708). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.

Repair route: open + save(); PDFium exposes no repair options. 5.14.0 untested.

name: zlib encoder replay (CPython zlib)
purpose: Re-deflate a candidate stream with the producer's zlib settings and compare to the stored bytes: a byte-exact verifier for Flate repairs.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/deflate_replay.streams.csv, research/experiments/results/deflate_replay.summary.json; 676 original and 63 damaged streams). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `python -c 'import zlib; print(zlib.ZLIB_RUNTIME_VERSION)'` in the scratch venv -> 1.3.
rationale: Exact replay of 228 of 333 Save As streams (68%; level 6 with memLevel 9: 220, memLevel 8: 187) but 1 of 343 Print to PDF streams (OBS-0703), corroborating OBS-0303 (54% across all Save As originals). Replay is a strong verifier for a candidate fix (GAP-154) but a poor locator: the first mismatch lay within +-2 bytes of the damage in only 4 of 22 replayable damaged streams (GAP-150). Adopt as the verifier for replayable producers; use preflate-rs (TOOL-366) for the rest. Chair note (2026-10-05, committee 004): the 68% comes from a memLevel {8, 9} grid. With memLevel 1-9 swept, stock zlib 1.3 reproduces 2,074 of 2,074 sampled Save As streams (OBS-0901), so WP-3.3 uses the full sweep.

name: python-zlib-ng (zlib-ng)
purpose: Second encoder family for replay.

rationale: Replayed 0 of 333 Save As and 1 of 343 Print to PDF streams (OBS-0703): neither REPDF producer uses zlib-ng, so it adds nothing as a replay oracle (GAP-154).

name: preflate-rs
purpose: Bit-exact DEFLATE re-creation with a small correction diff: describes any producer's encoder and can verify a repaired stream.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/deflate_replay.streams.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `pfprobe s0.zz s1.zz s2.zz` on 3 Flate streams of '<REPDF>/original/saveas/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(saveas).pdf' -> 'ok ... true' (exact round trip) for all 3, corrections 178, 96 and 290 bytes. <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
rationale: Exact round trip on 674 of 676 original streams (343/343 Print, 331/333 Save As), median corrections 125 and 49 bytes (OBS-0703), so it covers producers stock-zlib replay cannot (GAP-154; extends OBS-0303). On damaged streams it parsed 50 of 63 (all Adler-only, none of the 9 hard errors) with corrections larger than the original's in 39 of 50 (median ratio 1.84): correction size is a damage signal for locating the flip (GAP-150). Pure Rust, Microsoft, Apache-2.0 (SRC-0339). Chair note (2026-10-05, committee 004): TOOL-366 is the crate entry and TOOL-476 the zero-correction replay use of it; both are Trial and are read together.
alternatives: TOOL-476 (same crate: zero-correction replay as a verifier; this entry covers round trip with corrections)

name: gzrt (gzrecover)
purpose: Block-restart DEFLATE recovery tool.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/gzrecover_probe.csv; 63 damaged C9 streams). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `gzrecover -h </dev/null` -> 'Usage: gzrecover [-hpsVv] [-o <outfile>] [infile]'.
rationale: Copyleft (GPL), and not useful here: on 54 Adler-only streams its output still held wrong bytes in 9 (it often stops early); on the 9 hard errors it recovered 0 bytes in 8 (OBS-0705). Block restart cannot help single-block streams (OBS-0707, OBS-0301, GAP-152). Techniques only (SRC-0314).

name: infgen
purpose: DEFLATE disassembler: block structure and the exact decoding fault of a damaged stream.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/deflate_tools_probe.csv; 63 damaged C9 streams). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `infgen -h` -> 'infgen 3.6'.
rationale: Parsed all 54 Adler-only damaged streams to the trailer with unchanged block counts (damage confined to one block in 54), and named the DEFLATE fault in all 9 hard errors ('distance too far back', 'literal/length code is oversubscribed', ...) (OBS-0707). A cheap, permissive diagnostic for GAP-150/152; not a recovery tool.

name: rapidgzip
purpose: Parallel gzip/DEFLATE decoder with block-boundary resynchronization.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/deflate_tools_probe.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: import in the scratch venv -> rapidgzip 0.16.0.
rationale: Hazard: returned 'ok' on all 54 Adler-only streams and emitted wrong bytes in 53 without surfacing a checksum error; raised RuntimeError on all 9 hard errors (OBS-0707). Silent wrong bytes are exactly GAP-151's risk. Its resynchronization targets large multi-block gzip files (SRC-0303), not small single-block PDF streams (OBS-0301).

name: ZipRec (Brown 2011)

verification_evidence: Not run; no release located. Licence from the brief and memory.
rationale: GPL code: cite techniques only (SRC-0300). Its block-level resynchronization has nothing to restart at in most PDF Flate streams, which are a single block (OBS-0301, OBS-0707, GAP-152).

name: pugz

verification_evidence: Not run: the repository URL could not be resolved without authentication (git ls-remote, 2026-09-27).

name: DeepDiff over qpdf --json=2 (structural diff)
purpose: Structural diff of original vs repaired object graphs.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.summary.json, structural_diff). Re-checked 2026-10-05: rv3.py, DeepDiff(qpdf --json=2 --json-stream-data=none of '<REPDF>/original/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print).pdf', of the qpdf-rewritten C2 file) -> values_changed 209, iterable_item_added 312, iterable_item_removed 367 (identical to 2026-09-27).

A structural metric needs object-graph canonicalisation first (page order, fonts per page, XObjects, annotations, outline, as WP-3.2 lists), then a diff (GAP-008).

name: FaithC4 planted-token faithfulness benchmark (gwanglee/DoVLMsRead)
purpose: Planted-token test of whether a text recoverer reads or rewrites: the template for a fabrication metric.
license: Apache-2.0 (repository); dependencies include PyMuPDF 1.24.10 (AGPL) and python-Levenshtein (GPL-2.0-or-later)
verification_evidence: Not run. LICENSE, README and requirements.txt read from the repository on 2026-09-27.
rationale: The source of the planted-token idea (SRC-0422): 1,455 single-page documents in 4 conditions, per its README. No existing tool measures fabrication and omission against the upper bound (charter section 2), so we build it: plant rare or nonce tokens in our own generated documents, damage them, and score recovered vs planted tokens with rapidfuzz, without vendoring its AGPL/GPL-dependent scorer (GAP-201, GAP-055).

name: Flexible character accuracy (FCA)
purpose: Reading-order-tolerant character accuracy for repaired text whose order may differ.
verification_evidence: No implementation found: PyPI names flexible-character-accuracy, fca, ocreval, ocrevalUAtion, page-eval checked 2026-10-05 (SRCH-0705); 'fca' is Formal Concept Analysis.
rationale: Needed because repairs can reorder text blocks and plain CER then punishes order instead of content (GAP-008). The measure's definition (Clausner, Pletschacher and Antonacopoulos, ICDAR-era) is from memory and not yet sourced; implement it over rapidfuzz alignments and check dinglehopper's repository head first.
alternatives: rapidfuzz token-set ratios as a crude stand-in (TOOL-372)

name: python-Levenshtein (Levenshtein)
purpose: Edit-distance library.
verification_evidence: Not installed; licence from PyPI's JSON API (SRCH-0700).
rationale: Copyleft; rapidfuzz (TOOL-372, MIT, same maintainer) gives the same distances. FaithC4's scorer (TOOL-379) depends on it, so swap it when adapting.

name: Tesseract OCR
purpose: OCR of rendered pages: reference text and text-from-render comparison.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.ocr.csv). Re-ran 2026-10-05 on 19 originals in textlayer_coverage.py (research/experiments/results/textlayer_coverage.csv, OBS-0708): `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1 tesseract <200 dpi PDFium render> - -l eng --psm 3`, tesseract 5.5.3.
rationale: CER 0.0-0.04 against complete text layers at 1.0-1.3 s per page on one thread, about 5x faster than docTR (OBS-0706). It found 2 of 19 Print to PDF pages whose text layer holds only 50-60% of the visible text (OBS-0708), so a REPDF-style text reference must come from OCR of the original render or the upper bound, not the original's text layer alone (GAP-008). A classic LSTM recogniser without a generative language model, so a low rewrite risk (GAP-201).

name: docTR (python-doctr)
purpose: Deep-learning OCR on CPU for a second OCR vote.
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.ocr.csv); tool absent after the 2026-10-05 restart; Stage 4 re-verifies.
rationale: CER 0.0005-0.027 on pages with complete text layers, 6.1-7.2 s per page, model load 2.2 s (OBS-0706): a second OCR whose agreement with Tesseract can flag OCR errors in the reference; heavier because of torch (GAP-008).

name: VLM OCR models: olmOCR-2-7B-1025, LightOnOCR-2-1B, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, DeepSeek-OCR-2
purpose: Vision-language OCR as a possible text-from-render reference.
version: olmOCR-2-7B-1025 (8.29B params); LightOnOCR-2-1B (1.0B); PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (0.96B, GGUF build exists); DeepSeek-OCR-2 (3.39B)
verification_evidence: Not run; Hugging Face model metadata only (SRCH-0704). No weights downloaded (each is over the 1.5 GB limit).
rationale: Not shown feasible on 4 CPUs: autoregressive page transcription with 1-8B parameters would take far longer per page than Tesseract's 1 s (estimate, not measured). Their language priors can rewrite text, which is the very error a faithfulness metric must catch (GAP-201, SRC-0422). If one is ever tried, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6's GGUF build is the cheapest CPU timing trial.

name: CPR (BeenyHail/CPR) corrupted-PDF recovery baseline
purpose: The published font-aware recovery method (SRC-0123) as the comparison baseline before P5.
verification_evidence: Step 1 ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/cpr_step1_smoke.csv) on the 20-file seeded sample, after patching 28 Windows path literals in a temp copy and putting fontTools' ttx on PATH; Step 2 (FontDB + llama3.1:8b) not run. Checkout still in scratch; not re-run 2026-10-05.
rationale: Non-commercial licence (CLM-0700): run only as a research comparison and never copy its code. Step 1 word recall 0.69-0.82 on C1-C7; against the null baseline (PyMuPDF on the corrupted file) it is lower on C1-C3 and C7-C9, higher on C4 and C6, and mixed on C5; C10 0.0 (0.51 and 0.19 with glyph names normalised); CER often above 1 from duplicated text (OBS-0704). No deterministic mode: the LLM call sets no temperature or seed (CLM-0701), so charter FO-B3 needs a documented local patch (options temperature 0 and a fixed seed). Step 2 needs the 4.9 GB model (TOOL-386) (GAP-009, GAP-201).

name: Llama 3.1 8B via Ollama (llama3.1:8b, Q4_K_M)
purpose: The local LLM CPR's Step 2 uses to judge candidate CID-to-Unicode mappings.
verification_evidence: Not downloaded (over the 1.5 GB limit). Size, parameters and licence from the Ollama registry manifest on 2026-09-27 (SRCH-0704). Container: nproc 4, 15 GB RAM.
rationale: The 4.9 GB Q4_K_M weights fit in 15 GB RAM beside CPR. CPR asks it for a one-character O/X verdict on whether a candidate mapping reads as natural language (Code/cmap_error_P.py), so a language prior decides the output: the GAP-201 risk. The manifest sets only stop tokens, so Ollama's default sampling applies unless CPR is patched (CLM-0701). Throughput on 4 CPUs was not measured; prompt evaluation of roughly 200 tokens per call should take seconds per call (estimate from memory), times an unknown number of calls per document.
